title: quest agents --check reports state: current while the opum-quest plugin is disabled and no skill file exists, so --require-installed cannot distinguish a plugin-shipped skill from no skill at all (DEC-238 a3)
description:
Filed from DEC-238 (a3), opum-doc ruling 2026-10-25T06:54:02Z (record: opum-doc PR chore/dec-238-a2), which says verbatim: "quest-cli files the parallel bug: `quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude` reports current while the plugin is off."

MEASURED in this checkout on 2026-10-25, before filing:
$ quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude
plugin:
  id: opum-quest@opum
  remedy: claude plugin enable opum-quest@opum --scope user
  runtime: claude
  scope: user
  state: disabled
  version: 0.13.0
skill:
  state: current
state: current
exit=0

Corroborating state: `claude plugin list --json` reports opum-quest@opum enabled=false scope=user; `.claude/skills/` does not exist at all; `.lore/config.toml` sets skill_source = "plugin". So no quest skill file exists in this checkout, while the check concludes `current` and exits 0.

WHY THIS IS THE LORE DEFECT PARALLEL: for lore, a disabled plugin means the skill is absent, and `lore agents --check` exits 0 anyway — which DEC-238 (a2) (1) corrected by making the diagnostic lines the criterion rather than the exit code. Here the same exit code carries the same non-signal: `state: current` is reported while the plugin is disabled and no skill file exists.

WHAT IS DOCUMENTED, so the plan does not misread this as a regression: `quest help agents` (QCLI-371) says `data.plugin` reports installed/disabled/not-installed/not-detectable and that plugin state only reports and prints a remedy; it also says plainly that neither changes the exit code. `skill: state: current` under skill_source = "plugin" plausibly means "declared plugin-sourced, nothing to generate", which is consistent — but the top-level `state: current` is then read as "the workspace is current" in a checkout where there is no skill at all.

DECISION NEEDED AT PLAN TIME, and it is opum-doc call, not this repository own: whether `--require-installed` should account for a disabled plugin, or whether the output and help must state that `state: current` describes the managed CLAUDE.md block only. DEC-238 (a3) fixes the surrounding fact that quest guidance reaches workers through each CLAUDE.md managed quest block, and that no repo-local quest skill is restored (ODOC-142 retired it); re-enabling opum-quest is the operator call under DEC-172 (4bf), not part of this fix.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The `quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude` output states that `state: current` covers the managed CLAUDE.md block only, not plugin enablement, in both the human and the --json forms
The exit code is unchanged by a disabled plugin: QCLI-371 semantics are preserved and no carve-out is introduced for DEC-172 (4bf)
A test pins the disabled-plugin case and its exit code, so the output shape and the wording cannot change silently
`quest help agents` and the manifest text for --require-installed and data.plugin match the output wording
The change neither enables opum-quest nor restores a repo-local quest skill: DEC-172 (4bf) keeps the plugin off at user scope, and DEC-238 (a3) leaves quest guidance on the managed block

definitionOfDone.text: The fix lives in the check or its documentation, not in this repository CLAUDE.md
QCLI-371 exit-code semantics are either preserved deliberately or changed with the help text updated in the same change
The measured before-state from this record is re-run after the change and cited both ways

implementationNotes:
DEC-238 (a4) Point 3, opum-doc ruling 2026-10-25T07:18:35Z (record: opum-ai/opum-doc#1355, lands on dev when green), RULED A, verbatim: "the exit code is unchanged, and the output states that `state: current` covers the managed block only, not plugin enablement. B is not adopted: it would fail every fleet checkout while opum-quest is off by the operator DEC-172 (4bf), forcing a carve-out or a reversal."

So the arm this task implements is the reporting arm, not a semantic change: the check keeps exiting 0 with a disabled plugin and says what `state: current` is a statement about. Criteria 1-4 encode exactly that; criterion 5 records the boundary B would have crossed.

Measured before-state, 2026-10-25T07:01Z (to be re-run after the change, both ways):
  $ quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude
  plugin: id: opum-quest@opum, remedy: claude plugin enable opum-quest@opum --scope user,
          runtime: claude, scope: user, state: disabled, version: 0.13.0
  skill: state: current
  state: current
  exit=0
  $ claude plugin list --json  ->  opum-quest@opum enabled=false scope=user
  $ ls .claude/skills/         ->  No such file or directory
  $ quest help agents          ->  data.plugin reports installed/disabled/not-installed/not-detectable
                                   and "neither changes the exit code" (QCLI-371)

IMPLEMENTED on branch fix/QCLI-531-agents-state-scope, 2026-10-25. Change is output text only, per (a4) RULED A: no exit-code semantics touched.

1. src/cli/main.ts, the single agent.instructions-status output site (shared by --check and --update-instructions): data now carries stateScope: "managed-block" beside the existing state/skill/plugin fields. A comment names the ruling.
2. src/cli/main.ts help details for `quest agents`: new stateScope entry saying data.state reports the managed instructions block in the target file only and is not a statement about plugin enablement, which data.plugin carries separately and which never changes data.state or the exit code.
3. test/qcli371-marketplace-plugin-check.test.ts: a new test per runtime (claude, codex) that init-writes the block, then with a disabled plugin asserts --json gives state current, stateScope managed-block, plugin disabled and exit 0, and that the human form carries `stateScope: managed-block`. The file harness now parses JSON lazily on access, so a human-form assertion does not fail on non-JSON stdout; every existing assertion in the file still passes.

MEASURED against this checkout with the dev build (bun src/cli/main.ts), opum-quest disabled at user scope:
  human:  ... skill: state: current / state: current / stateScope: managed-block        exit 0
  json:   state=current, stateScope=managed-block, plugin.state=disabled, skill.state=current
          top-level envelope keys unchanged: contractVersion, data, kind, principal (last), schemaVersion
Before the change the same invocation printed no scope line and carried no stateScope, with the same exit 0: that is the non-signal (a4) RULED A removes.

VALIDATION: bun run check exit 0 under bun 1.4.3 (repo pin 1.4.2, no 1.4.2 on this machine): typecheck, lint, format, layer, 1317 unit tests in 147 files, 45 mod tests in 3 files. The local mod arm reports NOT TYPECHECKED for Claude Code 2.1.309 (no declaration on this machine, pre-existing).

REOPENED for DEC-238 (a6), opum-doc ruling 2026-10-25T13:19:22Z (record: opum-ai/opum-doc PR on chore/dec-238-a6), relayed by the lead. Q1 RULED A, refined, verbatim: "FINDING accepted: the printed `--scope user` remedy fails (\"already enabled at user scope\") under a local override. That is a real bug. ... the remedy names the SCOPE WHERE THE OVERRIDE LIVES: .claude/settings.local.json gets `claude plugin enable opum-lore@opum --scope local`; .claude/settings.json gets `--scope project`; a user-scope disable gets `--scope user`."

Approved line shapes to adopt with opum-quest@opum (coordination with lore-cli under LCLI-765, one PR per repository):
- `plugin-claude-override <file> (<scope> scope) sets opum-quest@opum to disabled, and wins over the user-scope row`, plus an additive JSON field;
- `agents-coverage ... covers the managed block and the skill file only, not plugin enablement`;
- `agents-skill-reachability no quest skill is reachable in this checkout` (exact quest wording to be confirmed with lore-cli).
Exit code unchanged per (a5). This amendment supersedes the `stateScope: "managed-block"` field shipped in #678 if the coverage line carries the same statement; that call is recorded when the bytes are agreed.

The printed remedy bug is REAL here too, measured 2026-10-25: `.claude/settings.local.json` sets opum-lore@opum=false while `claude plugin list --json` reports that plugin at scope=user, so an enable remedy printed with `--scope user` targets the wrong row.
finalSummary:
Per DEC-238 (a4) Point 3 RULED A, the output now says what its state verdict is about: agent.instructions-status carries stateScope = "managed-block" in both the human and --json forms, and the `quest agents` help states that data.state reports the managed instructions block of the target file only, never plugin enablement, which data.plugin reports separately and which never changes state or the exit code. Exit-code behaviour is deliberately unchanged. Verified with opum-quest disabled at user scope: human output ends `state: current` / `stateScope: managed-block` at exit 0, JSON carries stateScope beside state, skill and plugin, and the top-level envelope keys are unchanged with principal last. A per-runtime test pins the disabled-plugin case (state current, stateScope managed-block, plugin disabled, exit 0, and the human line), and bun run check exits 0: typecheck, lint, format, layer, 1317 unit tests and 45 mod tests. No plugin is enabled and no repo-local quest skill is restored, per DEC-172 (4bf).

DEC-238 (a6) reopened this task for wording alignment after #678 landed. The remaining work moved to QCLI-532, its child: the stateScope field shipped here is removed in favour of the agreed agents-coverage sentence, and the plugin remedy now names the override file scope instead of the listing row scope. This task delivery is unchanged: #678 made the state verdict say what it covers, and (a6) changed the wording rather than the behaviour.

Exit code unchanged throughout (DEC-238 (a5)).
